about: Repairs pack-check applies for a cause proven in a real run. A repair names a kind of fault, never a mod: loader and minecraft "*" (every loader and version), a match read from the jars before the game runs (mod-below, mod-range, mods-together, dependency-unmet, dependency-missing, bundled-in-use; "*" for any mod), the check that shows the fault in the game ("when" names a check the game must show before the match is more than a warning), an action, the evidence, and a test. General actions (replace-dependency, add-newer-bundled) find the jar when the repair runs, from Modrinth by the SHA-1 of a jar the pack carries, checked against its SHA-512 and its own metadata; add-jar, remove-mod and replace-mod name theirs. Every entry's test (jars, and the loader and version a general one runs on) must match before the action and not after it (run by self-test). The repaired pack runs beside the shipped one and is applied only when it passes where the shipped pack failed. A finding with no entry here is reported with its evidence and left alone.

fixes.symptom: A world opens the first time and never again: "Failed to load datapacks, can't proceed with server load", caused by a dimension's saved settings the game rejects on the next start.
fixes.cause: A library the loader takes from inside another mod's jar is older than the library's own release that fixed what it saves; the copy bundled in the mod writes data the game cannot read back.
evidence: pack-check on Prehistoric World 2 2.4.0 (Forge 47.4.20), 2026-10-30: Traverse 7.0.12 bundles Biolith 1.0.1-alpha.1; the second start fails; with 1.0.1-beta.1 added the second start opens, every placed block reads back, and a world saved by the broken version opens too

action.how: Each library in use from inside another jar gets its newest release for the pack's loader and game version as its own jar: the Modrinth project of the bundled jar (by its SHA-1, else the mod id as slug), checked against Modrinth's SHA-512 and its own metadata (the same mod id, a higher version).

fixes.why: Loaders take the highest version of a library that is both bundled inside another mod and present on its own, so the newer jar in the mods folder replaces the bundled copy. The repaired pack runs beside the shipped one and is kept only if it passes where the shipped pack failed.

test.from: Traverse 7.0.12 for Forge bundles Biolith 1.0.1-alpha.1 (Prehistoric World 2 2.4.0)

fixes.symptom: The game does not start: the loader stops because a mod requires a library version the pack does not have (an exact pin on an older release, while the pack takes the newest).
fixes.cause: A mod pins a library to one version and the pack carries another, so the loader refuses to start.
evidence: soulslike-weaponry-1.2.4-1.20.1-forge.jar and 1.3.1 META-INF/mods.toml: projectile_damage versionRange="[3.2.2+1.20.1]"; 1.4.4 has no projectile_damage dependency

pack-check --fix on JoJo's Bizarre Modpack 1.0.0 (Modrinth .mrpack, Forge 47.4.3, 108 files), 2026-11-14: the shipped pack's server stops at start-up and its log names soulsweapons; the repaired pack, run beside it, makes a new world, places 4,515 block items, opens the world again and reads all 4,474 placed blocks back; the fixed .mrpack it writes passes pack-check on its own

action.how: The library in a version every dependant in the pack accepts, from the Modrinth project of the pack's own jar for it (by SHA-1, else the mod id as slug), newest first; checked against Modrinth's SHA-512 and its own metadata. The pack's own jar of the library is taken out.

fixes.why: Replacing the library keeps every mod of the pack; updating the mod that pins it would change its content.
